transcript.text: The back burner on our gas hob has gone a lazy yellow colour and leaves black soot on the pan. What's wrong with it?
What is the main thing the hobs is doing wrong?

The rear left burner on my Smeg gas hob has a yellow, floppy flame instead of a blue one, and it's leaving black soot on my pans. It's been like that for the past couple of weeks. The other three burners look normal and blue.
No problem — let's take it one step at a time. When you start a programme, what happens that shouldn't, or what doesn't happen that should?
It's a gas hob, so there's no programme as such. The only thing wrong is the rear left burner's flame, which is yellow and floppy and leaves soot on the pans. Do you need anything else from me?
What is the main thing the hobs is doing wrong?

The main problem is the rear left burner, which has a yellow, floppy flame and leaves black soot on the pans. I've also noticed a faint smell of gas near the hob a few mornings, even when all the knobs were off. Is that something I should be worried about?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
If you can smell gas, treat it as an emergency: don't turn any switches on or off and no naked flames. Turn the gas off at the meter / emergency control valve if you safely can, open doors and windows to ventilate, and leave the property if the smell is strong. Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 and have a Gas Safe registered engineer check the appliance before using it again.
